quest.title: Book of Esoteric Revelations
quest.description: To investigate the secrets of the unfathomable book, you decide to work alongside Canotila...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Strange Part x1

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you doing under a waterfall? Are you gonna take a bath or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, if that's the case, we won't disturb you...
What bath? I am pondering some profound questions. If I must say... I suppose I am "meditating."
If you hadn't come thundering along and interrupted my train of thought, perhaps I would have already come up with the answers.

choices.text: "Meditating"...

response.text: I read in a book that if you run into something you can't make sense of, if you just "meditate," maybe you'll find the answers. I didn't misunderstand that, right?
Let's see... A human most strange and a rainbow balloon. You two must be from outside the village?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right! Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}... Wait a sec. Though you're right to say that we're not from here, what do you mean, a rainbow balloon?
Oh, right. You might not see it that way... I almost forgot about that again...
#Let me think... Right. {NICKNAME}, what does Paimon look like to you?

choices.text: She looks like a white Specter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! Don't people use "Specter" as an insult!?
Haha! Interesting. But to my eyes, Paimon is just like a little rainbow balloon floating in the air, and her string seems to extend upward, to somewhere above the sky itself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the... Seriously!?
#Yes... And just what does {NICKNAME} look like to your eyes, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Of course, Paimon's golden-haired traveling companion! Don't tell Paimon you see something else.
What I see... If I really must say, then I see a monster that looks like it could swallow the whole world in a single bite.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's way too scary! Are you serious!?
Of course I'm serious! Perhaps you've heard that we Melusines can see things that humans cannot see...
But for some reason, I see things differently, even when compared to other Melusines. I can always find things that have been hidden.
I have read that the "nature" of things is hidden beneath them, and this "nature" decides their "future." Not that I know what that means...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If that's the case, how did you know that we're outsiders?
Well... Though what we see is different, we can still find "ideas" that we have in common.
Just like how you can tell a flower is still a flower, no matter how strange the color, right?
As long as I spend enough time with everyone, I can grasp the "concepts" that everyone talks about and then pretend to fit in.
If you hadn't looked special in my eyes at all, I wouldn't have struggled to find the right "concept" to describe you.
As I thought. It seems that I still have lots to learn...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That's a whole bunch of stuff that Paimon didn't really get. On that note, we've been talking for ages, but we don't even know your name!

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: What is a name, but an artificial code that confers false uniformity on different perceptions? ... Still, everyone calls me Canotila, and you may do so as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! You talk in such a roundabout way, just like a scholar!

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Roundabout? Is that how you see it...

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: I don't usually talk with humans from outside, so I don't quite understand your methods of communication. I am merely making deductions and inferences based on what I have read in books.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You keep talking about what you've read in books... Do Melusines read too?

choices.text: It must be really inconvenient for you to turn the pages, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But maybe they don't use their hands, but the feelers on their heads... Er, um, wait, that's not the point!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon wasn't expecting there to be books hidden here.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Yes, an amazing scholar left them behind, all hidden inside a secret base. All of what I just said, I learned from those books.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: There's even a book there that I just couldn't understand. "Meditation" has allowed me to comprehend it — ever so little of it.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: But lately, I've been making no progress no matter how I rack my brain. That's why I came here to meditate and try to find a way forward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A book that can't be understood... Aren't arcane secrets, never meant to be known by anyone, usually encrypted in books like that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of secrets, that usually means treasure...! Now that Paimon thinks about it, she's getting curiouser and curiouser!

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: If you're interested, why don't I take you there to have a look?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: That book is important to me, and I must find a way to understand it.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: You appear to be knowledgeable, well-informed outsiders. Perhaps you'll be able to understand that book quite easily.

choices.text: I've certainly solved a puzzle or two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're like, super professionals at this! Come on, Canotila, show us the way!

choices.text: Our experience tends to be more on the practical side.
I wasn't expecting there to be books here.
Like emergency food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that's just wrong!

choices.text: Paimon's Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That sounds right, but it also sounds like you didn't answer that question at all.

choices.text: We're really sorry...

talks.objective: Go to the place where the book is hidden

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Aaand we're here! If we dive down below this "entrance," we'll find the place where that scholar once hid the books.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... But it looks like an ordinary pond. What sort of entrance are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Ah, right, it is being hidden, after all, so you won't be able to see... Hehe, just watch, then.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Canotila takes out something that looks like a key, tracing the air along some unseen trail.\nThere is a soft chime, and the shallow pool before you suddenly becomes unfathomably deep.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Well, here's the entrance now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon couldn't tell how you did that!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Well, I can't quite explain it either... But while others can't see it, there are actually all sorts of fissures here.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: As long as I use my token to draw a line across those fissures, I can do some incredible things.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: That said, I don't know why they are only present here. As such, I did a lot of research... until I found that indecipherable book...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: It has much to do with me and my token, and I'm also certain that if I figure it out, I'll know why I'm special in this way.

choices.text: That's quite the burden.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Well, then! That's enough of that! Let's go inside!

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: I must find a way to understand that strange book.

choices.text: There's nothing wrong with being special.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Awesome! Let's put another page in now, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Insert Page

talks.objective: Go to the place where the book is hidden

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Even when "meditating," I can't make heads or tails of what comes before and after.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: As such, though I can understand just a little bit, I still don't know what it is really saying... If I'm not mistaken, however, the book is still missing a lot of content.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The notebook does mention a few locations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So you mean that these locations might be clues?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Locations? Yes, the names of locations are written between important sections. Could it be trying to tell us where critical parts of the text are hidden?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: I mean, I've guessed as much in the past, but I've never left Elynas, so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, why don't you stay here, Canotila? We'll go investigate the places in the notebook. Maybe we'll find the missing pieces!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And besides, it's related to Elynas, so there's no way we're going to ignore it!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Alright! In that case, I'm counting on you two.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: If you find anything, just bring it back. I'll be waiting here for you.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: If we can find the missing parts of this book and put them back where they belong, maybe we'll be able to understand more...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: And then we just need to concentrate and "meditate" on the book, like before.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The edges of the page gradually blur. After a spell of dizziness, the words seem to become clearer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! This time, even Paimon could start to understand! Seems like the confusion was all due to the pages that were missing before, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Hmm, based on my previous results, that scholar must have been conducting research on Elynas or something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Then this book must record things that happened a long time ago!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Yes. But I still can't understand exactly what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you start meditating again, you once more attempt to understand the page's contents.\nThe edges of the page blur, and the incomprehensible shapes that line it leap forth, as if mounted on a pop-up book.\nYet, before you can make sense of what is happening, there is a rush of noise all around you, and you return to the world as it was.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon can read the words now, but the author's intended meaning is still a total mystery!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: We'll just have to put this last page in and see what we get. Maybe the contents will link up, or something!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you read faster and faster, you fall into a trance and arrive again in that mysterious space.\nThe same voice from before rings out.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "...No matter how many times I run the calculations, the results are the same. After a few hundred years, all the birthing waters of the world will dry up, and a few hundred years after that, the world will become as it appears now before us. This is quite the predicament."\n"...Hey, come on now, don't cry! There's nothing to be afraid of. I'm here, aren't I? Don't you trust me? Also, Alain and the others will definitely help. Also, I bet you'll definitely be able to survive in this world. You're special..."\n"...I know, I know. You're worried that constitution of others is different from yours. That's reasonable. Well, that's why we need to continue researching the things left behind by the Golden Troupe. Perhaps we'll discover some new possibilities. We'll go back to the Narzissenkreuz Institute together and take a look, okay?"

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The voice drifts away again. After what feels like a long time — though, in this world, time seems to no longer measure changes in matter — you hear the voice once more.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "It looks like he won't help us anymore. You're the only one I can rely on now. Hey, come on! Don't be like that. I'm sad too, but I won't cry until after the fat lady sings. Moreover, we still have to find a way to cure him."\n"...Don't be scared, it'll all go smoothly. There are already lots of people willing to listen to us. If we want to persuade them further... Besides belief, we'll also need ceremony..."\n"...As for the name, we'll call it the 'Book of Revealing,' and put it in the form of a book. We'll use our secret cipher to write it. Everyone only sees the world that their cognitive framework allows them to see. But using this method, we can share the visions we have foreseen with others..."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Just as you begin to listen closely to what the voice is saying, it begins to gradually fade away...\nAt the same time, you feel the world around you suddenly begin to collapse, and with a roaring sound resounding, you wake again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Are you okay, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was that an earthquake just now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Earthquake? What earthquake? Nothing happened here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon did get a little dizzy, but you looked like you'd fainted! You didn't wind up in some mysterious space again, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just what's going on with that weird space, anyhow... And if you think about it, it's pretty dangerous too! What if you go in and can't get back out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So just what did you encounter inside?

choices.text: I seem to have witnessed a premonition that someone had.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? The pages we found before did mention something about deductions and calculations, too... Could it be that the things revealed inside that space were actually the result of such deductions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... If what you say is true, then this was actually a book of prophecies, wasn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why make the format so complicated? If the author didn't want people to understand it, wouldn't it have been better to not write it at all?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Actually, I also heard all kinds of sounds while I was meditating... But they were just the songs of birds and flowers... I don't know anything about the prophecy you spoke of.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: It seems we must enter that space again to understand what is going on... If we meditate together this time, we should be able to enter it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's still worried... Wait! Paimon wants to come too! No way is she gonna stay here alone.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Once again, you focus upon meditating, and the furor surrounding you fades. The world grows silent.\nThen, you hear the tiniest of sounds, and a feeling that is wrath, or perhaps grief, wells up within your heart.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Your very soul feels drawn to this mysterious sound.\nAnd as you follow that sound, a whole world — utterly alien, supremely familiar — races to meet you.

choices.text: I seem to have heard a prophecy that someone made.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Did someone say anything in there? And it was some kind of prophecy? That's real creepy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wha—? Where the heck did we end up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is like some kind of dreamscape! This must be the strange place you were talking about before.

choices.text: It's much more vivid than before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did the author of the book really create this place? And they hid such a big space inside it, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Well, Paimon doesn't know how they did it, but this place looks like a ruin!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, we meditated with Canotila to get here, but we're the only two people around right now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She didn't fall somewhere, did she? Oh no! Things could get bad if she winds up in danger!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go find her! Hurry!

choices.text: It could be dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Where'd Canotila go? She was just here a moment ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! There's something on the ground, pick it up and take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You pick up a page from a book...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this page the same as the ones we found before? How did it end up here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's easily readable! Is it because we're in this strange space?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cataclysm? Destruction? Some kinda apocalypse? What...? Even if Paimon can read the words, it still doesn't make any sense.

choices.text: But if we put it together with the other pages...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... That's true. We've definitely seen something about "calculations" before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, does this mean that this is the future the author wants us to see?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A world where even Sweet Flowers and Mints won't grow — ugh, that's a terrible place no matter how you slice it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if that really is the future, shouldn't the author tell everyone about it and find a solution? Why make a place like this?

choices.text: Maybe this is the only way everyone will believe it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It also mentions some kind of "Looking Glass"... Seems like there are other ways to get in here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Paimon doesn't think any of this will be much help in answering Canotila's questions...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, forget it! Who cares about some dumb prophecy, anyway? The important thing right now is to find Canotila! Let's keep looking!

choices.text: Or maybe he had his own considerations.
This appears to be a prophecy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... So it's as we guessed previously.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No sign of Canotila or where she's gone. There's only this fellow here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That said, it doesn't seem to want to attack us anymore. That's a first for a Rifthound, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like... It wants to say something to us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not that we can understand it, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We shouldn't get too close... just in case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is Paimon seeing things?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's an ordinary little doggie doing here? Where'd that Rifthound go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, take a look! Is there something wrong with Paimon's eyes?

choices.text: It might be the Rifthound.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it trying to tell us to go through that passage over there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Judging from its reaction, Paimon guessed right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knows where that's gonna lead, but we weren't able to find Canotila anywhere... so maybe she did leave via that way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And it looks like there's no other route we can take, so let's just try it and see what happens!

choices.text: Anything can happen in a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. We came right back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or maybe... we never even left...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Oh? You had the same reaction as I did, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Canotila! We were looking all over for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon kept calling out for you, but you never responded! That place was so dangerous, but you just ran around all over the place!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Dangerous? The place we entered was so serene and peaceful, like a beautiful garden.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But all we saw was rubble!

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: That's odd. I kept looking for you two back in that previous space. But there were big trees and flowers everywhere, so I got lost...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: Fortunately, I followed the sound of a bird, then found a golden butterfly, which brought me up on top of the garden...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about the Rifthound? We saw you and a Rifthound... Oh, right! That Rifthound even turned into a dog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Now it feels like Paimon is just talking nonsense...

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: I saw a little dog too! On top of the garden, there was a cute little dog that nodded at me, and helped open the way out for me.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: I thought you both had gone somewhere else to play... And that I didn't need to worry, so I just came back here.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: And you? What did you discover?

choices.text: Nothing special.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Though Paimon doesn't think it'll answer your questions, we did find a page...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You open the page you found, and show it to Canotila...

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: The butterfly... It's the golden butterfly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: I can see golden butterflies flying out from the page, just like the one I saw in the space before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Never mind solving anything, we've got even more problems on our hands now! Seems like you really did see something completely different in that space!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. If that space is the future predicted by the author, then why did you see a garden? Just thinking about that makes Paimon's head hurt!

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: But I was very happy inside... I didn't even think about those questions! Maybe that's what the book was trying to tell me all along.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Even if we perceive differently, if we can communicate our feelings to one another, maybe the "essence" of things doesn't matter all that much after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wouldn't say that we had a great time in there, but if you've figured things out for yourself, good on you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, that place is pretty sketchy, and we don't yet have any clue as to what's up with that prophecy either.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Speaking of the prophecy, this book makes it sound really scary, sure, but what if the things I saw were the real future? After all, such things aren't set in stone, are they?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: And since the book mentions other ways to enter that space, we may be able to figure this book and its prophecy out if we find them.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: And then maybe we can meet there again, in that space!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, it might be better if we just meet in reality. Also, Canotila, don't go running around in that space anymore!

choices.text: We found another page.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! We found this inside, though we don't know if it'll be useful, it also looks like a page from this book...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... So you can't understand it at all either, after all?

choices.text: Not a single word.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe there's some kind of cipher! Take a closer look!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You stare at the runes on the page for some time. The runes slowly start to disintegrate and reassemble themselves, becoming new words.\nAt the same time, your surroundings seem to recede, and you arrive in a strange new place.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "I see. This is a world where even Sweet Flowers and Mint cannot grow. Can you see it, too?"

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You turn around to look for the source of the voice, but are suddenly awakened. Looking back at the book, it looks just like it did originally, as though nothing happened.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #So... Did you discover anything, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: It was like I entered a strange place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A strange place? But you were here the whole time! Did you just stare too intensely or something?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: I knew you'd be able to see it too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Have you had the same experience, Canotila? Is this what you meant by "meditating"?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Yes. Though I can't understand a single word in the book, I get a strange feeling from looking at it for long enough.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: It feels as though you've been transported to another world, and then, you can start to understand the book's contents.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: But as soon as you awake, you're back to being unable to comprehend it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then what have you seen before...?

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Oh! Wait just a moment.

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Ta-da! This is my notebook. I've written down everything I saw inside!

response.speaker: Canotila
response.text: Um, that said, I wrote it all down while I was "meditating," and I was sort of in a trance, so it might be a bit hard to understand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Yep, this is really messy. Wow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it says something about an "Elynas" or something like that...

choices.text: I think I saw the runes dissolving, and then reconstructing themselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's weird... Did you just stare too intensely or something?

choices.text: I reckon we should look more closely.

dialogues.speaker: Canotila
dialogues.text: These do look like the missing pages from the book! Let's try putting one back in, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Insert Page
